open_points.subject: A18 rule 3 store order
open_points.text: “records have one order” and “their position in the store's one order of records” do not define which records receive positions, whether the order is global across record types, or whether a lifecycle update changes a record's position
open_points.question: What exactly is the store order, and is a record's position permanently assigned when it is first created?
options: One global immutable creation sequence for every record
A separate sequence per record type
Every creation and lifecycle update receives a new position
open_points.default_guess: Use one global monotonically increasing position assigned once when each record is created; updates do not move it.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 3 multi-record transactions
open_points.text: “one transaction inside it” leaves no order for several records created by the same transaction
open_points.question: In what order are positions assigned when one store call creates several records atomically?
options: A fixed record-type and item order specified for each store call
The order in which the implementation inserts them
All records in the transaction share one position with a secondary key
open_points.default_guess: Specify a fixed insertion order for each store call and assign distinct consecutive positions.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 3 change boundary
open_points.text: “Every change is one call to the store module and one transaction inside it” does not define what constitutes one change when an action creates or updates several related records
open_points.question: Which groups of record and file changes must be atomic in one store call, and which may be split across calls?
options: Each surface action is one transaction
Each lifecycle transition is one transaction, with explicit multi-record groups
The generated modules choose transaction boundaries
open_points.default_guess: Treat each logically indivisible lifecycle transition as one transaction and explicitly list its record group.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 3 request serialization
open_points.text: “Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive” does not define when a concurrently delivered request has arrived
open_points.question: What event establishes the total order of concurrent MCP requests?
options: Completion of receipt of the whole request message
Acceptance by the MCP transport
Assignment of a sequence number by a single dispatcher
open_points.default_guess: Assign a monotonic sequence number in a single dispatcher after the complete request has been received.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 3 interrupted requests
open_points.text: “one request ... ends before the next begins” is silent about a client disconnect or cancellation while its request is executing
open_points.question: Does an executing request continue to completion after its caller disconnects, or is it aborted before the next request begins?
options: Continue the request and commit its result
Abort only before its first store change
Abort immediately and roll back what can be rolled back
open_points.default_guess: Continue an accepted request to completion; loss of the response does not undo its actions.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 1 process lock
open_points.text: “takes an exclusive lock in the data directory” does not say whether the lock is process-held and automatically released, how a stale lock artifact is treated, or when the lock is released
open_points.question: What lock mechanism and lifetime establish that a crashed process cannot permanently block a later start?
options: An operating-system advisory lock held for the process lifetime
An exclusive-created lock file with explicit stale-owner recovery
A database-level exclusive lock
open_points.default_guess: Use an OS advisory lock held from the beginning of startup until process exit, with automatic release on crash.

open_points.subject: A18 rules 1–4 startup
open_points.text: The text says the kernel locks, checks privacy and links, opens its store, cleans files, and A14 recovers runs “on start”, but gives no common order for those steps
open_points.question: What is the exact startup order, and which failure is reported when several startup checks fail?
options: Lock, validate directory, open and validate database, clean files, recover runs
Validate directory, lock, clean files, open database, recover runs
Another explicitly fixed sequence
open_points.default_guess: Lock first, validate the directory tree, open and validate the database, perform cleanup, then perform A11/A14 recovery before opening the surface.

open_points.subject: A18 and A14 startup interaction
open_points.text: A18 removes “the spool directories of runs that ended and do not keep their spool” while A14 says stored run status may lag its records and is derived again at startup
open_points.question: Does A18 decide which spools to remove from the pre-recovery stored status or from the status derived by A14, and does cleanup occur before or after recovery advances running runs?
options: Derive statuses first, clean eligible spools, then advance running runs
Clean using stored statuses before recovery
Complete all recovery and advancement before spool cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Convert in-flight attempts and derive statuses first, remove spools based on the derived state, then advance runs left running.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 2 data-directory creation
open_points.text: “The data directory holds one SQLite database” is silent about an absent data directory, an absent database, an empty directory, or a database with an unknown schema
open_points.question: Which of these states initializes a new store, and which refuse startup?
options: Create the directory and database when absent
Require the directory but create a database only when it is empty
Require a fully initialized compatible store and refuse every missing component
open_points.default_guess: Require an existing private data directory, create a new database only when no store exists, and refuse an incompatible existing database.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 2 privacy
open_points.text: “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user” gives no exact ownership or permission test
open_points.question: What owner, file-type and permission conditions make the directory, database, content area, spool, temporary files and SQLite auxiliary files private?
options: Owned by the kernel user with no group or other permissions
Owned by the kernel user with no group or other write permissions
Rely only on effective access checks
open_points.default_guess: Require ownership by the kernel user and no group or other permission bits on every component.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 2 permission changes
open_points.text: “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise” specifies only a startup response and is silent when ownership or permissions change after startup
open_points.question: Are privacy conditions rechecked on later store accesses, and what happens when a component has become non-private?
options: Recheck every opened component and fail that store call
Check only at startup
Stop the kernel when a later violation is detected
open_points.default_guess: Open components safely and recheck ownership and mode on each access; fail the call without record changes and stop after returning an internal error.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 2 symbolic links
open_points.text: “Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links; a link found at start stops the start” does not say whether the startup scan is recursive, includes directory components, or covers unknown entries
open_points.question: Exactly which directory entries and path components are checked for symbolic links at startup and on later access?
options: Recursively check every entry and every component below the data directory
Check only known database, value, fixture and spool paths
Check only final path components when opened
open_points.default_guess: Recursively reject every symbolic link and open every traversed component without following links.

open_points.subject: A18 rules 3–4 failed calls
open_points.text: Rule 2 says a later symbolic link “makes that store call fail with nothing written”, while rule 3 says “the only trace it can leave is a published file no record names” for a failed call
open_points.question: May a store call that fails because it encounters a symbolic link leave an already-published orphan file, or must that specific failure leave no filesystem change at all?
options: The symbolic-link rule is stronger and requires cleanup of every file published by that call
The general orphan-file exception applies to symbolic-link failures too
open_points.default_guess: Make the symbolic-link rule stronger: the call must leave neither record changes nor a published orphan.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 4 publication durability
open_points.text: Files are “flushed” and “then renamed into place”, but the text does not require syncing the containing directory or define SQLite journal and synchronous settings
open_points.question: What durability protocol must make the promised crash behavior hold across power loss, including consistency between a published file and the database record naming it?
options: fsync the temporary file, rename it, fsync the parent directory, then durably commit the referencing record
Rely on ordinary flush, rename and SQLite defaults
Commit the record before publishing the file and repair missing files at startup
open_points.default_guess: Durably publish and directory-sync the file before a SQLite transaction durably commits any reference to it.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 3 transaction outcome
open_points.text: “A call that fails writes and changes no record” is silent about an SQLite commit that returns an error with an uncertain durable outcome or an error after the commit has succeeded
open_points.question: How does the store classify and recover a call whose commit outcome is uncertain, so it does not report failure after changing records?
options: Treat any uncertain commit as fatal and determine the result during restart before serving requests
Report failure and permit recovery to discover a committed change
Configure the database so an uncertain commit cannot occur
open_points.default_guess: Stop the process on an uncertain commit and reconcile the durable database state during startup before answering another request.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 4 overwrite rule
open_points.text: The formal invariant says “file_published -> ... never_overwritten”, but the normative text permits “a spooled file no record names ... [to be] replaced at its position” and says a later write may replace it
open_points.question: Does `never_overwritten` apply only to completed files named by records, or also to orphan spooled files?
options: Only files named by committed records are immutable; unnamed spool files may be atomically replaced
Every published file is immutable, so retries must use a new path
open_points.default_guess: Limit the invariant to files named by committed records and allow atomic replacement of unnamed spool files.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 4 existing digest target
open_points.text: “Equal bytes are stored once” and “a completed file a record names is never overwritten” do not say what happens when the target digest path already exists but its bytes, size, type or file kind are wrong
open_points.question: Must an existing digest-named object be revalidated, and what happens if it does not match?
options: Fail the call and refuse startup thereafter as store corruption
Quarantine and replace the object
Trust the filename without reading it
open_points.default_guess: Validate the existing regular file's digest and size; treat a mismatch as fatal store corruption and never overwrite it.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 4 deduplication scope
open_points.text: “Equal bytes are stored once” follows rules for value bytes, file fixtures and spooled files without saying which areas share deduplication
open_points.question: Are equal bytes deduplicated only within the content-addressed value/fixture area, across values and fixtures together, or also across run spools?
options: One shared content-addressed blob for values and fixtures; run spools remain positional copies
Separate deduplication for values and fixtures; no spool deduplication
Global deduplication including spooled files
open_points.default_guess: Deduplicate values and trial fixtures in one content-addressed area, but keep each run's spool positional and separate.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 4 orphan fixture cleanup
open_points.text: Startup removes “value bytes no record names”, but a failed call can publish a trial file fixture before its TrialCase record exists, and unnamed fixture bytes are not explicitly listed
open_points.question: Are unreferenced file-fixture blobs removed at startup under the same rule as unreferenced value bytes?
options: Remove every unreferenced blob in the shared value/fixture area
Remove only value blobs and retain unreferenced fixture blobs
A fixture is not published until its TrialCase record can commit
open_points.default_guess: Remove every unreferenced blob in the shared content-addressed value/fixture area.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 4 cleanup failures
open_points.text: Only a spool directory that cannot be removed is explicitly allowed to remain; the text is silent when removal of a temporary file or an unreferenced value or fixture fails
open_points.question: Does failure to remove each other startup-cleanup target stop startup, get deferred like spool removal, or get ignored?
options: Stop startup for temporary and content-area cleanup failures
Continue startup and retry all cleanup on a later start
Continue only when the inaccessible item cannot be served
open_points.default_guess: Stop startup when a temporary or unreferenced content blob cannot be removed; only ended-run spool cleanup is explicitly non-blocking.

open_points.subject: A18 store integrity
open_points.text: The rules state that completed files named by records exist and are complete, but do not say what startup or a read does when the SQLite database is corrupt, a named file is absent, or its digest differs
open_points.question: How does the kernel respond to database corruption or a committed record whose referenced bytes are missing or corrupt?
options: Refuse startup after a full integrity and reference check
Start, then fail only the store call that encounters the damage
Delete or reconstruct the damaged record or bytes
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup on database corruption; validate referenced files when accessed and stop on any missing or mismatched committed object.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 4 temporary-file recognition
open_points.text: “On start, temporary files ... are removed; nothing else is” does not define how a file is recognized as temporary rather than as an unknown persistent file
open_points.question: What names and locations identify temporary files, and what happens to an unrecognized entry in a managed store directory?
options: Reserve a fixed temporary namespace and refuse startup on every unknown entry
Reserve a fixed temporary namespace and preserve unknown regular files
Treat every unreferenced file as temporary
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed temporary names in dedicated directories; remove only those names and refuse startup on unknown entries in kernel-managed areas.
